messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated tail latency detected for /v1/decode streaming in prod-us-west-2. p95 ~ 320ms (norm ~85-95ms), p99 ~ 980ms, error rate +4.8% over 5m. Auto-failover to degraded pool executed.

oncall-alex: I'm taking this. Paging SRE + runtime. Any customer reports?

sre-maya: seeing heavy kernel stalls in traces tied to compilepath 2.1.4 rollout. Flame graphs show long waits in kernel launch and small, frequent GPU allocations.

runtime-vik: confirmed. The TRT8/FlashAttn binary from 2.1.4 enabled `-fuse-fast-kernel` by default. Hypothesis: increased register pressure -> intermittent GPU pagefaults on older instance types.

infra-ryan: infra telemetry: node pagefaults spike on subset (gpu-pool-3). Memory reclaim and mm counters high. I'll cordon suspect hosts.

oncall-alex: Mitigation plan (immediate): 1) disable fast-kernel path via runtime env var, 2) route streaming to dedicated low-latency pool for sensitive customers, 3) prepare rollback if hotpatch fails. Who can run the env hotpatch?

runtime-vik: I can. Hotpatch steps (canary first):

```
# runtime admin steps
hotpatchctl set-env --cluster prod --env REDWOOD_COMPILE_FLAGS="-no-fast-kernel"
hotpatchctl restart-slices --cluster prod --selector compilepath=2.1.4 --graceful
```

I'll apply canary to two nodes and watch p95/p99.

oncall-alex: Go for canary. Post results here.

runtime-vik: Canary applied to gpu-pool-3-node-7 and -9. Logs: replacing fast kernel with fallback. Sample trace: decode id=0xabcde pre-p95=410ms post-p95=110ms.

sre-maya: great signal. If canary holds, roll out. I'll monitor pagefault and mm counters.

deployment-bot: deployctl: starting hotpatch rollout: 20% slices every 30s (12/120 slices).

oncall-alex: dashboards show global p95 down to ~130ms within 8m of canary. p99 trending down. Error rate back to +0.6%.

support-julie: CS: contacted AcmeSearch (top customer). They reported timeouts around 02:10 UTC for long streaming sessions. Case INC-4532 created.

product-zoe: flagging customer comms. Will update status page and notify impacted accounts.

infra-ryan: cordoned gpu-pool-3-node-4 and -5 for maintenance. Removing from LB.

runtime-vik: after rollout, kernel telemetry shows nvrtc timeout counts dropped, alloc stalls decreased. Mitigation effective across affected slices.

oncall-alex: decision point: full rollback to 2.1.3 vs keep 2.1.4 with fast-kernel disabled. Thoughts?

infra-ryan: rollback is heavier; prefer keeping 2.1.4 but mark it degraded and ship a 2.1.4.1 patch that turns fast-kernel off by default and puts it behind a feature toggle. Schedule rebuild of fast kernel with reduced register usage.

sre-maya: agree. We'll block further 2.1.4 rollouts and add extra QA focused on older GPU variants. Add regression tests for long streaming sessions.

support-julie: AcmeSearch confirms improvement after mitigation. We'll leave ticket open for monitoring.

oncall-alex: Summarizing for postmortem / handoff: Root cause: `-fuse-fast-kernel` in compilepath 2.1.4 increased register pressure -> paging on older GPUs. Mitigation: hotpatch to set `REDWOOD_COMPILE_FLAGS=-no-fast-kernel` + routing to dedicated low-latency pool. Impact: p95 ~90ms -> ~320ms, p99 up to ~980ms, error rate +4.8%. Affected long streaming workloads; AcmeSearch reported timeouts. Next actions: mark 2.1.4 degraded, ship 2.1.4.1 with toggle, rebuild kernels, add QA.

product-zoe: I'll draft customer note and post incident banner.

sre-maya: filing internal incident ticket INC-4532 and attaching traces + flamegraphs.

runtime-vik: adding repro steps and microbench harness used for register measurements into the incident doc. Will own kernel fix.

oncall-alex: Closing paging loop — will hand off to morning SRE. If tail latency creeps up again, re-page immediately. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:\"

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed by oncall at 4060013950 after SLOs met for a 10m window.

oncall-alex: final metrics: pre-mitigation p95=318ms, p99=972ms, errors +4.8%. post-mitigation p95=118ms, p99=220ms, errors +0.4%. Attaching dashboards to postmortem.

sre-maya: assigning owners: runtime-vik (root cause & repro), infra-ryan (deploy/rollback process), product-zoe (customer comms).

support-julie: closing customer ticket; AcmeSearch reports stable at 02:45 UTC.

oncall-alex: Handoff done. Ping me overnight if anything looks off. Good work team.
